subject: geography

parts.part_text: What is the angle of inclination of the earth’s axis with its orbital plane?
parts.answer_text: The angle of inclination of the earth’s axis with its orbital plane is 66 ½º.
parts.final_answer: The angle of inclination is 66 ½º.

parts.answer_text: Rotation is the movement of the earth on its axis. Revolution is the movement of the earth around the sun in a fixed path or orbit.
parts.final_answer: Rotation is about the axis, while revolution is around the sun.

parts.answer_text: Earth takes 365 days and 6 hours to complete a revolution. But, for the sake of convenience, we consider that a year consists of 365 days. The six hours that are ignored make one day (24 hours) over a period of four years. This one day is added to that year in the month of February. Therefore, after every four years February has 29 days and that year is known as leap year.
parts.final_answer: A leap year has 29 days in February, occurring every four years.

parts.part_text: Differentiate between the Summer and Winter Solstice.
parts.answer_text: Summer Solstice is when the rays of the sun fall directly on the tropic of cancer, and the North pole is tilted towards the sun, resulting in summer in the Northern Hemisphere. Winter Solstice is when the rays of the sun fall directly on the tropic of Capricorn, and the North pole is tilted away from the sun, resulting in winter in the Northern Hemisphere.
parts.final_answer: Summer Solstice occurs in June, while Winter Solstice occurs in December.

parts.answer_text: Equinox is the position of the earth when direct rays of the sun fall on the equator. At this position, neither of the poles is tilted towards the sun so, the whole earth experiences equal days and equal nights.
parts.final_answer: During an equinox, day and night are of equal length.

parts.part_text: Why does the Southern Hemisphere experience Winter and Summer Solstice in different times than that of the Northern Hemisphere?
parts.answer_text: The Southern Hemisphere experiences Winter and Summer Solstice in different times than that of the Northern Hemisphere because when the North Pole is tilted towards the Sun, the Northern Hemisphere experiences Summer Solstice, while the Southern Hemisphere experiences Winter Solstice. Conversely, when the North Pole is tilted away from the Sun, the Northern Hemisphere experiences Winter Solstice, and the Southern Hemisphere experiences Summer Solstice.
parts.final_answer: The solstices are opposite in the two hemispheres due to axial tilt.

parts.part_text: Why do the poles experience about six months day and six months night?
parts.answer_text: The Poles experience about six months of day and six months of night because of the tilt of the Earth on its axis. When the Northern hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun, the North Pole is inclined towards the sun, it experiences continuous daylight for six months. These conditions are reversed when the South hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun.
parts.final_answer: The tilt of the Earth causes extreme variations in daylight at the poles.
